There is no need to treat “50+” as an exact total or as a contradiction of 67. A collection with 67 vehicles also has more than 50. When discussing the event, the announced 67-car figure is the more precise reference.

Check the in-game Collection for the roster you can see in the current beta. The announced total is helpful context, but it does not show which cars you personally own or provide a permanent list for every future update.

sections.heading: How You Get Cars
paragraphs: Lucky Crates are the starting point in the official how-to-play instructions. Spawn and buy a crate, place it, and open it for a car. Then add the vehicle to your Collection to complete the earning part of the sequence.

This makes the relationship easy to follow: the crate is what you begin with, and the car is what the opening provides. Follow the current interface for the purchase and opening rather than assuming a fixed crate price from a separate guide.

If you are looking for a particular vehicle, use the live Collection and any information the game displays. The public description does not publish a model-by-model drop table, so a general car count should not be turned into a guaranteed opening result.

links.label: Learn how to obtain cars from Lucky Crates

sections.heading: Add Cars to Your Collection
paragraphs: After obtaining a car, add it to the Collection. The official instructions say this is when earning starts, so the Collection is a functional part of progression as well as a way to understand your cars.

The developer also advertises money generation while offline. That connects your collection with progress between active play sessions. When you return, check the current Collection and money display before choosing another crate.

Do not assume a car’s earnings from its appearance or from a guessed rarity category. Use the information shown in the current game. This guide explains the Collection’s confirmed role without assigning invented income statistics to individual models.

sections.heading: Driving Cars in Drive World
paragraphs: The official DRIVE WORLD event adds an entirely new massive map and says all 67 cars are drivable. It also advertises x3 Hatch Speed while driving, connecting the driving activity with the crate side of the game.

Roblox lists the event for October 2–4, 2026. Check the current game page when entering, especially after that window. The announcement does not by itself promise that every event feature will remain permanently available.

The phrase “all 67 cars are drivable” describes the announced feature. It should not be read as a promise that all 67 are automatically in your personal Collection, or as a detailed claim about vehicle handling. Use the live game to see the cars and options available to you.

sections.heading: Racing and Car Cleaning
paragraphs: The Roblox description advertises all-or-nothing racing with friends. This is another way cars fit into the game beyond opening crates and adding vehicles to your Collection. Read the current prompts before joining a race so you understand the choices on screen.

ASMR Car Cleaning is also an advertised feature. It gives players another car-focused activity to explore. The description names the feature without publishing a detailed cleaning checklist or reward schedule, so follow the current game interface.

The developer additionally advertises 5+ Car Edits. Explore those in the game rather than assuming a named edit list or a tuning system. Edits, cleaning, and racing broaden the car theme without replacing the official collection-and-money loop.

For a first session, it can help to finish the basic crate sequence and then explore an activity that interests you. That is a simple way to understand the game before trying to compare every feature at once.

sections.heading: About a Full Dream Car Collection Car List
paragraphs: The current official pages confirm the car count and core car features, but individual model names can change as the beta updates. Use the in-game Collection for the live roster.

A useful car list needs actual model names from the current game. The public car-count announcement is not a substitute for that roster, and this page does not turn the 67-car number into an invented table of names, rarities, or stats.

If your goal is to decide what to collect next, start with the vehicles shown in your current Collection interface. If your goal is driving, check the live event options. These two tasks use the same car theme but ask different questions about what you can do in a session.
The beginner guide can help if you need to return to the basic sequence. Obtain a car from a crate, add it to the Collection, and keep building toward the vehicles you want.

faq.question: How many cars are in Dream Car Collection?
faq.answer: The base description advertises 50+ cars; the official Drive World event says all 67 current cars are drivable. Check the in-game Collection for the live roster.

faq.question: How do I get cars in Dream Car Collection?
faq.answer: Spawn and buy a Lucky Crate, place it, and open it for a car. Then add the vehicle to your Collection.

faq.question: Can cars make money while I am offline?
faq.answer: Yes. The official description confirms offline money generation, and the how-to-play instructions say adding cars to the Collection starts earning.

faq.question: Can I drive every car in Drive World?
faq.answer: The official event says all 67 cars are drivable. Check the current game page for event access and the live interface for your available cars.

faq.question: Can I race friends?
faq.answer: Yes. The developer advertises all-or-nothing races with friends; read the current game prompts for the session rules.

faq.question: Can I clean cars?
faq.answer: Yes. ASMR Car Cleaning is an advertised feature of the Roblox game.

faq.question: Is there a complete official car list?
faq.answer: The public pages cited for the count do not provide a full model-by-model roster. Use the in-game Collection for current individual car names.
